section_summary: This section concerns suspected Japanese intelligence activity in Argentina. U.S. Embassy and FBI documents discuss Masao Tsuda, Ángel Perrone, Kingo Kawai, and Choko Shirakawa. Most of the section is a translation of Argentine police proceedings recording searches, testimony, and inquiries into the Domei agency and people linked to the former Japanese Embassy.

subfiles.title: Embassy cover despatch forwarding notes on Masao Tsuda
subfiles.about: Forwards two notes supplied to Argentina about Masao Tsuda.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Embassy's December 8 and 13, 1945, notes on Tsuda.

subfiles.title: Note verbale on Masao Tsuda
subfiles.to: Argentine Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship
subfiles.about: Describes Tsuda's Domei role and transmission of Allied war information to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy identifies Tsuda as Domei's principal South American representative and requests notice of Argentine action against him.

subfiles.title: Supplementary note verbale on Masao Tsuda
subfiles.to: Argentine Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship
subfiles.about: Reports an archival payment to Tsuda for a trip to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: A Japanese Embassy voucher records 600 Argentine pesos paid to Tsuda in June 1942 for an investigation trip.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Ángel A. Perrone
subfiles.about: Forwards information on a suspected Japanese intelligence courier.
subfiles.summary: Introduces an enclosed report on Perrone's Argentine newspaper work and suspected intelligence role.

subfiles.title: Report on Ángel A. Perrone
subfiles.about: Reviews Perrone's movements, employment, radio dispatches, and unsubstantiated espionage suspicions.
subfiles.summary: Sources traced Perrone's visits to Argentine government offices and his work for El Economista. His dispatches contained figures that might have carried a secondary meaning, but investigators found no such meaning.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Kingo Kawai
subfiles.about: Forwards findings on allegations of Kawai's espionage.
subfiles.summary: The FBI states that investigation did not substantiate allegations against Kawai.

subfiles.title: Report on Kingo Kawai and fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Examines allegations that Kawai and two fishing vessels aided Axis intelligence or submarines.
subfiles.summary: The report reviews Kawai's arrest, the vessels' radios, crew lists, and activity in Buenos Aires port. It says the espionage allegations against Kawai were unsubstantiated.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Choko Shirakawa
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Shirakawa's suspected clandestine correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Notes Shirakawa's alias and his family's internment in Córdoba Province.

subfiles.title: Report on Choko Shirakawa and clandestine correspondence
subfiles.about: Traces letters from Lima and Santiago to addresses associated with Shirakawa.
subfiles.summary: The report links correspondence addressed to Juan Roberto Martínez with Shirakawa's apartments and describes inquiries into its route through Taiho personnel in Peru and Chile. It also records Shirakawa's police questioning, acquaintances, and family internment.

subfiles.title: Foreign Activity Correlation handling note
subfiles.about: Restricts use of an attached FBI report.
subfiles.summary: Requires clearance with the division before citing the FBI report.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal of Argentine police reports
subfiles.about: Forwards translated Buenos Aires police reports on Japanese espionage inquiries.
subfiles.summary: The FBI requests that any use of the confidential translation conceal its source by paraphrase.

subfiles.title: Translation of Argentine police proceedings on suspected Japanese espionage
subfiles.about: Records searches, testimony, detentions, and inquiries concerning Domei and Japanese contacts in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The proceedings record statements from suspects, witnesses, and police employees, together with searches at residences and the Domei agency. They examine correspondence, telegrams, a possible code, a proposed explosive, and approaches concerning Pacific nautical maps. Several detainees were released when police found no serious charges; the translated proceedings continue beyond page 155.
